=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/security_audit.sh:3478-3481 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The audit dedupe still treats the first finding marker anywhere in an issue body as valid, so a body with no leading marker block but a marker later in its text suppresses filing that finding.
  WHY: The audit skips the finding as already followed up, but the review gate only recognizes markers in the leading block, so it reports `followups_missing` and holds the PR while later audits keep suppressing the follow-up (source severity MAJOR).
- scripts/security_audit.sh:3757-3765 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: `LAST_ANY_FOLLOWUP_BY_FILE` is built only from existing index-file entries and is not filled with issues created in the current run until the end, so new issues from this run are not used for cross-reference.
  WHY: If several new consolidated issues are planned for different files in one run, the `Depends on` calculation for the second file's issue will not see the first file's new issue, which can leave dependency chains missing or wrong (source severity MAJOR).
- scripts/security_audit.sh:3803 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The consolidated closed fallback through `LAST_ANY_FOLLOWUP_BY_FILE` depends on the index title column being kept strictly as `open` vs `-`, so a closed issue not marked `-` could be wrongly ranked as a closed predecessor.
  WHY: Dependency resolution is fragile because it depends on strict upkeep of the index file's title column, and nothing verifies that column (source severity NIT).
- tests/test_security_audit_workflow_contract.py:571-572, 590-591, 594-595, 606-607, 763, 792, 4191-4219 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The last run re-indented continuation lines and docstrings of existing tests unrelated to P5b, removed the unused `trusted =` assignment (line 763) and dropped an f-string prefix (line 792), which trips the PR's "Changed pre-existing assertions (removed_or_modified)" gate.
  WHY: Nothing fails at runtime because the assertions mean the same thing, but about 30 lines of re-indentation churn add review noise and fire the changed-assertions gate signal (source severity NIT).
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

  expected_change_site: scripts/security_audit.sh
  confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  EVIDENCE: The consolidated key built with `hashlib.sha256(str(finding["file"]).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()` treats findings in different files as different keys, so the code files one issue per unique file key (or per `multi:` group) and could produce several issues in one cycle instead of one.
